He collaborated with notable figures such as the Hanseatic League, which connected the Baltic and North Seas to the Mediterranean trade routes. This partnership enabled the exchange of goods, ideas, and technologies between the East and West, contributing to the growth of trade and commerce in the region.

Olbram III. von Škvorec's legacy extends beyond his business acumen, as he played a significant role in shaping the cultural and religious landscape of Central Europe. He was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Catholic Church, which had a lasting impact on the region's architecture, literature, and art.

In the annals of history, Olbram III. von Škvorec's contributions are remembered as a testament to the power of strategic partnerships and cultural exchange in shaping the course of human civilization.
